_about: Owned sources behind every dimension of ('mavic4pro', mesh revision 1). Plan B.0: no dimension without an owned source (spec, manual, our scan, CAD we hold, or an owned photo with a stated scale), and no third-party licensed mesh or number derived from one.
user_decisions_2026_09_18: Mavic 4 Pro IS included in revision 1.
The x1.59767 height stretch is KEPT and the shortfall recorded, because the B1 height round found the evidence cannot remove it (about 35 mm would be missing). Same treatment as mini5pro.

p.88 C2 table: 'Intelligent Flight Battery BWX341-6654-14.3, 62x44x128 mm, Approx. 331 g'

fcc_external_photos.what: FCC ID SS3-L3AB2410 External Photos, 23 laboratory frames with steel rules
fcc_external_photos.licence: US federal public record (FCC public inspection); no copyright claimed
used_for: p05 front elevation: one tapered landing leg per FRONT motor; gimbal hanging in front of the nose; motor can and gimbal block sizes (via the inventory round)
p07 bottom plan: leg count and position, battery bay forming the rear belly
p02/p05/p06: the B1 ruler-scaled multi-view fit (can diameter, tracks, can-base and stack-top heights, foot position)

p05 front elevation: the camera head's CORNER RADIUS, as a scale-free ratio R/W = 0.4502 (rms 2.97 px = 2.28 % of the head width over 63 image rows of the head's lower half, against 13.52 px for a square-cornered outline). Producer scratch mesh_rev1/b4/mavic4pro/work/gimbal_corner.py -> work/gimbal_corner_p05.json. Only the LOWER pair of corners is measured; the upper pair is behind the nose shroud in p04/p05/p06, so top/bottom symmetry is assumed and declared.
fcc_external_photos.caveat: the FCC unit is a pre-production (EVT) sample. Shape and internal layout are usable; surface finish and colour are not. Production-unit photos p08-p13 (Wikimedia Commons) are the reference for finish.

owned_top_photo.what: top view of the complete aircraft, arms unfolded, propellers unfolded
owned_top_photo.provenance: third-party parts-supplier product image (djioemparts.com watermark) held in our own photo set since the 2026-08-03 collection round; not a licensed mesh and no geometry is copied from it - only lengths are read off it
owned_top_photo.registration: work/measure_planform.py -> work/planform_c02.json. The four rotor axes are the midpoints of each propeller's two orange blade tips; the image axes are the aircraft axes to within 0.03 deg, so no rotation is applied; the scale 0.57912 mm/px is B1's ruler-scaled front track 363.92 mm over the measured 628.4 px front hub separation.
scale_cross_checks: propeller tip-to-tip 264.1 / 263.9 / 260.6 / 260.3 mm against the official 267.0 mm (the deficit is the orange tip patch's own centroid bias)
front track 363.9 + can 29.3 = 393.2 mm against the official unfolded width 390.5 mm
owned_top_photo.tolerance: +-3 mm on every width and span
used_for: shell x span and width stations
arm headings and arm width
gimbal plan footprint and its front face at x = +175.4 mm
the two nose-deck vision eyes at x = +88.9 mm, y = +-27.1 mm

b1_height_round.held_at: scratch wf/b1_height.md and mesh_rev1/height/work/m4p_height_ledger.json, m4p_fit.py, m4p_mc.py, m4p_variants.py
b1_height_round.method: 3 views, 40 Monte-Carlo draws plus systematic variants; scale from the ruler digits only; focal length pinned
used_for: motor can diameter 29.330 mm (variants 29.32-29.57)
landing-foot position (-0.41, +-184.88) mm against front can centres (0, +-181.96)
front/rear track 363.92 / 301.59 mm and fore-aft spacing 275.68 mm (DECLARED, not applied)
the height shortfall table
rotor_dirs (-1, +1, -1, +1) in rotor_deg order FL, RL, RR, FR: FL and RR clockwise seen from above
gimbal block height 64 mm from FCC p05 at 0.3964 mm/px (+-1-2 mm)
motor can Ø30.5 x 19.8 mm from the same view, as an independent cross-check
revision-0 realized metrics the budgets are set against

components.rev0: x span -114.2 ... +89.8 mm, width 118.08 mm (_SHELL_SHAPE fl 0.62 / fw 0.302 / cx0 -0.06, proportions of body_l_mm 329 and body_w_mm 391)
components.rev1: x span -72.5 ... +126.0 mm, 28 measured width stations, 68.9 mm at the waist and 92.1 / 86.9 mm at the rear / front shoulders Since 2026-09-18 the two bands the arm fairings hide carry filled-in stations every 10 mm (the spacing drone_parts_rev1.section_loft_shell already names as the plan's standard): the WIDTH there is still the same straight line between the measured sections either side, and (z_top, z_bot) come from the same revision-0 section law every measured station uses, so the crown and keel follow their declared source instead of being chorded across 39.0 mm. Chord error 1.594 -> 0.177 mm; 29 -> 34 stations.
components.not_measured: width for x in [+65, +104] and [-54.5, -30]: the arm fairings and the shell are one run in the top view there, so P1's straight ruled band between the measured sections either side is used

components.rev0: Ø45.86 mm (0.052 x 441 mm used as a radius) x 33.815 mm realized
components.rev1: Ø29.33 mm x 33.815 mm realized (height is revision 0's carry-over)
components.not_measured: the can height. Consistency note only: the inventory's un-stretched reading 19.8 mm x 1.59767 = 31.6 mm is within 7 % of the carried-over 33.8 mm

components.grade: medium-high for the position, medium for the size
components.rev0: squashed sphere of Ø60.0 mm raw (95.9 mm realized in z) centred at x = +89.8 mm, front face +106.9 mm, 65 % of its faces buried in the shell
components.rev1: 58.0 x 64.0 mm head, 45.4 mm deep, corner radius 26.11 mm (= 0.4502 x 58.0, measured on FCC p05), with a 30 mm diameter x 10 mm lens barrel; front face at x = +175.4 mm; floor at revision 0's realized -77.73 mm. The 0.4502 ratio makes the front profile an obround rather than a box, which is what every owned view shows.
components.source: owned_top_photo (position and width), inventory_round (height), fcc_external_photos p05 (corner radius, 2026-09-18), revision 0 (floor)
components.not_measured: the 64 mm height is one reader's reading of one FCC view; the block/barrel depth split and the 6 mm burial into the nose are construction; the UPPER corner radius is assumed equal to the measured lower one; and the cylindrical collar where the housing enters the nose (the 'Infinity Gimbal' housing named in assets/photos/mavic4pro/SOURCES.md) is not built, because no owned view gives its diameter or its length.

components.not_measured: the leg's own section, taper and splay - revision 0's width rule is carried over

declared_not_applied.measured: front track 363.92 mm and rear 301.59 mm (B1, ruler-scaled); the top photo reads 363.9 / 312.6 mm
declared_not_applied.why: plan B.0 freezes rotor xy at revision 0's realized positions. This is the largest xy error left in the mesh: +-10 mm on the front rotors and +-16 mm on the rear, i.e. 0.31 lambda at 5.8 GHz on the rear pair.

declared_not_applied.measured: B1 puts the rear can base 9.5 mm and the rear stack top 15 mm above the front
declared_not_applied.built: one plane for all four rotors
declared_not_applied.why: plan B.0 keeps the prop mount planes at revision 0's.

declared_not_applied.measured: reproduced by B1's front track 363.92 + can 29.33 = 393.25 mm
declared_not_applied.why: the same frozen rotor track. Reported, not gated.

declared_not_applied.measured: B1's FCC fit puts the tallest resting feature at about 100 mm (front can base 53.0, rear 62.5, front stack top 84.8, rear stack top 100.1, shell outline top 97.1 mm above the feet)
declared_not_applied.built: revision 0's realized vertical layout, giving the official 135.2 mm unfolded height
declared_not_applied.why: user decision 2026-09-18 plus the B1 finding: removing the stretch would leave the model about 35 mm (95 %: 32.7-37.3) short of the official height and no measured feature carries that 35 mm. The error is about +30 mm on the front can base, +22 mm on the rear, and +40 / +25 mm on the stack tops - and the stack tops are the rotor planes, where the micro-Doppler lives.

declared_not_applied.what: shell width inside the two bands the arm fairings hide
declared_not_applied.measured: nothing - x in [+65, +104] and [-54.5, -30] read as one run with the arm fairings in the top photo
declared_not_applied.built: the straight line between the measured sections either side, unchanged since the first build; the 2026-09-18 station fill changed only the crown and keel, which have their own declared source (revision 0's section law)
declared_not_applied.why: nothing is invented where the photo says nothing.

declared_not_applied.what: the gimbal's cylindrical collar into the nose, and its upper corner radius
declared_not_applied.measured: p05 shows a cylindrical housing where the head meets the nose shroud; the head's LOWER corner radius is measured as R/W = 0.4502
declared_not_applied.built: an obround-section head at the measured lower-corner radius, applied to all four corners; no collar
declared_not_applied.why: the collar's diameter and length are hidden in every owned view, and the upper corners are behind the shroud. Applying the measured radius to all four corners is an assumption of top/bottom symmetry, stated here.

not_used: Any third-party licensed mesh. No Sketchfab / 3dmodels.org / CAD-marketplace model of this aircraft was opened or measured.

The 'Mavic 3 hover RPM 4000-4700 measured reports' claim that the 2026-09-17 research round flagged as a fabricated cross-check. Hover rpm is unchanged at revision 0's 3600 and is not a geometry input.
The repair-blog claim of a magnesium-alloy core frame and carbon-reinforced polyamide arms (single secondary source, unverified). Material groups are unchanged from revision 0.
